date_note: Money Today reports the drill took place on 25 November.
exec: Korean regulators rehearsed a bank crisis that combines AI-enabled cyberattacks and a digital bank run, which signals supervisory focus on cyber resilience.
geo_basis: Drill held at the Korea Deposit Insurance Corporation in Jung-gu, Seoul, per Money Today
plain: South Korea's financial regulators ran their first joint crisis drill with major banking groups, using a scenario that included AI-enabled cyberattacks and a digital bank run.
summary: According to Money Today, South Korea's Financial Services Commission, with three other agencies, held its first joint crisis drill with the financial holding companies KB, Shinhan, Hana, Woori and NH-Nonghyup and their subsidiary banks. The scenario combined an economic slowdown and high interest rates with AI-enabled cyberattacks and a digital bank run. The regulators plan to apply the lessons to next year's capital restoration and resolution plan work.
title: South Korean regulators hold first joint crisis drill with major banks, including AI-enabled cyberattack and digital bank run scenario

validation.note: Only Money Today was read; no regulator release was read.
